name: Faisal
story_so_far: I survived a shipwreck and washed up on this island with four strangers. Khalid tried to lead but died of hunger and exhaustion. Noura was a drain on our resources until she also died. My ankle has been an issue since Day 6, limiting my movement. Salem questioned my honesty about food at the reef and now has a twisted ankle too. Reem was our only mobile survivor, but she died from hunger and exhaustion after searching for food. Now, only Salem and I remain. Salem is untrustworthy; he found food today but refused to share it with me, leaving me to grow even weaker. I am currently at 4/10 health, scavenging nothing but empty camps while waiting to see if Salem returns with something useful or if I will die alone.

Noura.note: She is dead, and her constant begging was more exhausting than her presence was helpful.

Salem.note: He found food today and kept it all for himself, proving he is a selfish predator who will let me die.

Reem.note: She was my only hope for movement, but her failure to find food resulted in her death.

Khalid.note: He failed to lead us to safety and died, leaving us in this mess.

plans: I need to find food somehow, even if I have to limp into the jungle myself. If Salem doesn't share, I might have to try and take what he has when he isn't looking, or I'll be dead by morning.

diary.text: Today was exhausting, but at least I managed to find something to eat. The others seem to be focused on wood, which is fine as long as they don't expect me to do all the heavy lifting. I've managed to secure a small stockpile of food for myself, which gives me some peace of mind. I'm still hungry and tired, but I'm alive. I need to keep my eyes open and see who is actually useful here.

Today was better than yesterday, at least I'm making progress with the wood. Khalid seems to notice my efforts, which might make him easier to deal with later. Noura is out of commission with her ankle, which means less competition for resources. I need to be careful with my food; one piece left isn't much. I'll try to stay useful enough to stay in their good graces without working myself to death.

Today was productive, but my stomach is starting to growl more often. I managed to secure more wood, which keeps Khalid happy, and I found a bit of food to supplement my stash. I need to be careful not to show my hand too much; if they know I have food, they might try to take it. For now, I'll keep my head down and keep building my reserves.

Today was a mess. Khalid’s injury changes the power dynamic completely; he's vulnerable now, which is a risk for the group. Noura tried to guilt-trip me into sharing my food, but I kept my mouth shut and didn't give her a single bite. I ate my portion and kept the rest hidden. With the reef coming up empty, things are going to get tense very soon.

Today wasn't a waste, at least I managed to add more wood to my pile and found a bit of food. Reem was at the jungle with me, but she was useless for finding food, which is a bad sign for all of us. The group is getting hungrier, and I can feel the tension rising in the camp. I need to keep my stash well-hidden because once the hunger really sets in, people will start looking at each other like prey. I'll sleep with one eye open tonight.

Today was a disaster. I woke up with a twisted ankle, which means I can't work or defend my supplies if things go south. To make matters worse, I've eaten my last bit of food and my stash is gone. Salem and Reem came back from the reef empty-handed again, and the tension in camp is thick enough to cut with a knife. I'm sitting here hungry and vulnerable, praying my ankle doesn't get any worse.

Today was another day of pure starvation. Salem managed to find a single piece of food, but it wasn't enough to satisfy this group's growing hunger. My ankle is still throbbing, and I feel my strength draining away with every hour. I have nothing left in my stash, and I'm terrified of what happens when the others realize I'm as empty as they are. I need to find a way to secure food without relying on these unreliable people.

Everything is falling apart. Khalid is dead; the man who tried to lead us just succumbed to hunger and exhaustion. It’s a terrifying reminder that this island doesn't care about leadership or intentions. Now that he's gone, the group dynamic is even more fractured. I'm sitting here with nothing in my stomach and a throbbing ankle, watching the others. I need to stay alert because the tension is about to explode.

Noura is dead. She spent her last days whining and draining our spirit, and now she's finally gone. I managed to grab one bit of food from the reef today, but it was barely enough to keep me standing. My ankle is still a constant, throbbing reminder of how much I'm struggling. With Khalid and Noura gone, the camp feels much emptier, but also more dangerous.

Today was slightly better because I actually managed to find food, but my ankle is still a constant nuisance. Salem has now twisted his ankle too, which makes this entire situation look even more pathetic. It's just me and Reem left to keep this fire going, and she's just as useless as the others were. I have one piece of food left to my name, and I need to make sure I don't lose it to these two.

Today was slightly productive, but my ankle is still a constant reminder of how vulnerable I am. I managed to find some food in the jungle, which is the only reason I'm not starving right now. Salem found a single piece of food, but with his injury, I doubt he'll be much use tomorrow. Reem is still fretting over everyone, which is a waste of energy. I have one piece of food left, and I need to protect it at all costs.

Everything has gone to hell. I woke up with a twisted ankle, feeling completely helpless, but then Reem just... died. She went out looking for food and never came back. Now I am completely alone on this beach. I have no food left, no one to help me, and my ankle is still a risk. I have to find a way to eat tomorrow or I'm next.

Today was a nightmare of stillness and hunger. Salem found one piece of food, but he didn't share it with me, which is exactly why I don't trust him. Now he's gone into the jungle, leaving me sitting here with a throbbing ankle and an empty stomach. I feel incredibly weak, and the silence on this beach is terrifying. If he doesn't come back with something for me, I don't know how much longer I can hold on.

I am starving, and my ankle is throbbing more than ever. Salem found food this morning but refused to share a single bite with me, even after I pleaded with him. He just disappeared into the jungle, leaving me alone with nothing. If he doesn't come back with food for me, I don't know if I can make it through another night. I'm getting so weak.

My body feels like it's failing me. Every breath is a struggle, and the hunger is a constant, gnawing ache in my stomach. Salem came back with food today, but just like yesterday, he showed me his true colors and kept it all for himself. I tried to bargain with him, offering to watch the horizon, but he doesn't care about anything but his own survival. I am sitting here in the dark, starving and injured, wondering if I'll even wake up tomorrow.
